Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:1: After explaining holiness, it is fitting to explain what pertains to it in practice, and we say that the matter of holiness in which we are commanded, "you shall be holy," is that a person separate himself from things that are profane, and sanctify his soul and his body - for the opposite of the profane is the holy, like the distinction of Shabbat, called holy, from the weekdays - and when we know what the holiness of Shabbat is, we shall know the matter of holiness explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:2: And behold, concerning the holiness of Shabbat, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, page 94a), in the distinction between "kodesh" [holy] and "mikra'ei kodesh" [holy convocations] - and he explained that Shabbat is the very essence of the revealed holiness, and concerning this it is said (Exodus 31:14), "and you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you." And he said that the secret of Shabbat is the secret of the son ascending to his father's house without permission - and this is (ibid. 15:11), "who is like You among the mighty, O LORD; who is like You, glorious in holiness" - and he says "in holiness" specifically, for he has already grown strong in his father, "glorious in holiness," but not yet prepared to be sanctified [as an independent entity]. And he further says on: Rabbi Yehuda said, the joy and protection of the day of Shabbat is in everything, because this day is crowned with Abba and Imma, and holiness is added to its holiness - which is not found this way on other days, for it is holy and is crowned with holy, adding holiness to its holiness - and therefore this day is the joy of the upper and lower beings, all rejoicing in it, full of blessings in all the worlds, all repaired from it - to this point. Behold, it is explained that the holiness of Shabbat is the light of the holiness of Abba and Imma revealed in Tiferet, and from there to all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:3: And further, concerning the holiness of Shabbat and the other days, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 204a), concerning the reality of Shabbat: they said that she is Malchut, a middle point for all six days, from which they nurse, and on the day of Shabbat she is the "bat ayin" [pupil of the eye] unified with the three Patriarchs, who are "shin" [numerically three] - and this is "Shabbat" - shin, bat [pupil]. And further, there is a supernal Shabbat, three Patriarchs bound to the pupil of the eye, and they are bound to the World to Come. And there is a still more supernal Shabbat, when all mentioned is bound to the supernal point, which is also the secret of the pupil of the eye - this is the summary of his intent. It follows that wherever the son ascends, the daughter ascends with him above, in such a way that the secret of the holiness of Shabbat is always the light flowing from Abba and Imma, and further still from above, from Atika, who is the root of holinesses, called the Holy Ancient One of Holy Ancient Ones, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:4: And so it is further explained in Parashat Vayakhel (Zohar, page 205a); they said there, concerning the secret of the marital timing of Torah scholars, from Shabbat eve to Shabbat - and they said, what is the reason? Because on all the weekdays there is another spirit resting on the world, and on this night there is another, supernal, holy spirit that descends to holy children - and that spirit blows from the Holy Ancient One of all ancient ones, and descends to the lower point, giving rest to all - and this spreads to all sides, above and below, as it is said, "between Me and the children of Israel" - to this point. And so they further say on there, the day of Shabbat is joy for all, and everything is elevated above and below, and the lower point shines to ascend above, in the beauty of crowns, seventy portions more, and the Ancient of ancients is aroused - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:5: And since Shabbat is the root of all holinesses, we say that what the Torah commanded, "you shall be holy, for I am holy," is that we sanctify ourselves and draw upon ourselves, every single day, from the light of the holiness of Shabbat - if we sanctify ourselves from doing labor and purify our thoughts, and the other particulars that will be explained concerning the holiness of Shabbat.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:6: And there is an allusion to this in the Zohar (Parashat Yitro, page 89a), in these words: Rabbi Yehuda said, certainly it is written (Exodus 20:8), "remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy," and it is written (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I the LORD am holy," and it is written (Isaiah 58:13), "and call the Sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honorable." We have learned, on this day all the souls of the righteous delight in the delicacies of the Holy Ancient One, the concealed of all concealed, and this spirit of delight spreads through all the worlds, ascending and descending and spreading to all holy children, all who keep the Torah, and they rest in complete rest, and all anger, all judgments, and all harsh services are forgotten from them - this is what is written (ibid. 14:3), "on the day the LORD gives you rest from your sorrow," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:7: And his intent, at the beginning of his words, saying "certainly it is written, 'remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy'" - the meaning is that on the day of Shabbat we are clearly warned to sanctify it, and its holiness is in our own sanctification - and so they said, of blessed memory, in the Mechilta (Parashat Ki Tisa), on the verse (Exodus 31:16), "and the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe [la'asot] the Sabbath": Rabbi Elazar ben Parta says, whoever keeps the Sabbath is as though he made [asah] the Sabbath, as it is said, "to observe [la'asot] the Sabbath" - to this point. And his intent is along the lines of what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bechukotai, page 113a), "and observe them" [ve-asitem otam] (Leviticus 26:3) - he says, what is "ve-asitem otam"? Rather, whoever performs the commandments of the Torah and walks in its ways, as it were, is as though he made Him above - the Holy One, blessed be He, says, it is as though he made Me - and they established this, and therefore "ve-asitem otam" - "you shall make them" indeed, since you are aroused to join one thing with another, to praise the holy Name properly - "you shall make them" indeed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:8: And let us return to the matter: for in saying "remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy," its holiness is certainly explicit - but for the other days, we have no proof that we need to sanctify them; and from what the verse says, "you shall be holy" without qualification, the intent is the holiness of all the days - and he brought "the holy of the LORD, honorable" to teach a verbal analogy [gezerah shavah] with "for I am holy," for just as the verse "the holy of the LORD, honorable" refers to the day of Shabbat, from its preceding "and call the Sabbath a delight," so what the verse says, "for I am holy," its intent is that everything be holy like the holiness of Shabbat - for Shabbat is the root of all holinesses. And therefore he brought the proof, "we have learned, on this day the souls of the righteous delight in the delicacies of the Holy Ancient One, the concealed of all concealed," and he said that on the day of Shabbat this light spreads through all the worlds, and therefore the day of Shabbat is holy of itself, its holiness not being in the hand of the court like the establishment of the festivals, as they explained, of blessed memory, in the Mechilta (Parashat Ki Tisa) - and this is what the verse says, "for I am holy," along the lines of what they explained, of blessed memory, in the discourse we copied in the previous chapter, saying, or does it mean only, if you sanctify Me, then I am sanctified, and if not, I am not sanctified? The text teaches, "for I am holy" - in My holiness I stand, whether they sanctify or do not sanctify. We find we learn, from the general sense of his words, that a person is obligated to sanctify the six days from the holiness of the day of Shabbat.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:9: And so it is further explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 204a), in these words: come and see, the supernal secret of the matter - all those six days, the matter of everything stands, unified in the secret of one holy point, and all the days are unified in it, and there are other days that stand outside on the other side, and there are other six days that stand within the holy circle and are unified in the holy point. And Israel, holy, and all those who occupy themselves with holiness all the days of the week, are unified - all those six days, in those six days within, which are unified in that point - they are unified in this, in order to be protected. And all those six days of Shabbat [i.e., of the week], that point is hidden; once Shabbat enters, then that point ascends and is crowned and unified above, and all are hidden within her. Come and see, there are days and there are days - weekdays, as explained, and these stand outside forever; the days of Shabbat, which are the days of the week, stand for Israel; and when this point ascends, everything is hidden away and she ascends - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:10: And his intent is that there are three kinds of days. The first, weekdays, which stand outside of holiness, for the idol-worshipping nations - the intent being that to the idol-worshipping nations were given thirty-nine labors, corresponding to the thirty-nine curses with which Adam, Eve, the serpent, and the earth were cursed, as explained, of blessed memory (Tikkunei Zohar, page 85a). Had man not sinned, he would not have needed to descend to this lowliness he is in, requiring him to plow and sow, but would have been in the Garden of Eden fulfilling "to work it and to keep it" through the fulfillment of positive and negative commandments in a spiritual manner, as will be in the future after the resurrection - for the Torah and its commandments are one forever - and when Adam descended, through his sin, to the husk, he was forced into these labors.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:11: And the Holy One, blessed be He, to purify and sanctify us so that we be cleaved, raised us from the six external days and gave Israel dominion over holy conduct through Metatron, who is the prince of the world - as it is said to Joshua (Joshua 5:14), "I am captain of the host of the LORD; now I have come" - for even though Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, pushed him away, he was forced to accept him, all the more so now in exile, when the conduct is through him, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 14b) and in other places (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 215a) - and the six weekdays, the conduct is through Metatron - so too explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 243b), and in the Tikkunim (page 2b), in these words: the bird, which is his bird, is Metatron - of him it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "for a bird of the air shall carry the voice" - the voice of the Shema, which comprises the six weekdays and rules over them, and takes that voice and flies with it up to the middle pillar - to this point. And so they further say on there, that through this agent they are unified in the six weekdays. And the term "six weekdays" is not precise along the lines we said in the discourse of Parashat Vayakhel, which said that weekdays are called "for the external ones" - rather the intent is that during the six weekdays, the world is conducted through the aforementioned prince, and through him our prayer ascends.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:12: And so he said in the Tikkunim, in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 106b), that concerning him it is said (Exodus 20:9), "six days you shall labor, and do all your work," in these words: on the weekdays, the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil ascends, which is Adam, "and He formed him with the good inclination and the evil inclination" - this is what is written (Genesis 2:7), "and the LORD God formed man" - and this is the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil that Adam sinned with, and this is Metatron, who is a servant that rules over the six orders of the Mishnah, and he is physical, and rules over the six weekdays, which are "chulin" [ordinary/profane] of impurity and "chulin" of purity - and from him were given the six orders of the Mishnah, in forbidden and permitted, impure and pure, valid and invalid; and concerning him, "six days you shall labor, and do all your work" - and there is no [true] service except prayer, in which a person must be like a servant arranging his praises before his master, and like a servant asking a reward from his master, and like a servant receiving a reward from his master and going his way. But on Shabbat, the queen who rules is the Tree of Life, not the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil - they established that the Tree is not to be used in any way [on Shabbat] - to this point. Behold, it is explained that the whole reality of the service of prayer is through this servant during the six weekdays; but on Shabbat, the light of Atzilut rules - and through this may be understood his saying (Exodus, ibid.), "and the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God" - that the whole intent of prayer should be in Atzilut, and Atzilut is clothed in Beriah, and this is "the LORD your God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:13: And incidentally it is explained that this servant is called the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil - and he says in the Tikkun (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 87b), "the Tree of Knowledge" - "good" is Metatron, "evil" is Samael. And Adam's sin was to mix the evil with the good, and therefore, in this matter, there are the six orders of the Mishnah, to separate the good for itself and the evil for itself. And so he says there (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash) further on: and the Tree of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil requires making a separation between good and evil - this is what is written (Genesis 1:4), "and God separated between the light and the darkness" - and one must make a cutting off in it, so that a person be without the evil inclination, along the lines of David, who cut it off from himself and killed it through his study, this is what is written (Psalms 109:22), "and my heart is wounded within me" - and corresponding to the forty-nine [aspects] of Metatron are the forty-nine pure faces, the forty-nine impure faces - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:14: And incidentally it is explained that the virtue of studying the Mishnayot is to kill and subdue the evil inclination - although these Mishnayot, which we have from the disputes of the Tannaim, did not yet exist in David's time, nevertheless he had six orders of Mishnah from settled halachot, and he studied them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:15: And behold, in the reality explained in this discourse, that Metatron is called "good and evil," and it is also said that he rules over the weekdays, and it is said that there is "chulin" of impurity and "chulin" of purity - along these lines, in the discourse of Parashat Vayakhel, there are weekdays among the external forces, and there are, within, the six days of the week, which are in purity for the conduct of Israel - and these two aspects are like a tree and its bark, good within and evil without, the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:16: And he says these six days are held in the holy point - it appears from the wording that this point is the Shechinah, hidden within Metatron, within the Heichal of the bird's nest, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 102a) - and Metatron comprises six chambers corresponding to the six days of creation, and in the seventh chamber the Shechinah is hidden; and during the six days of creation, the Shechinah is a point hidden within those six mentioned days, and the days shine from her, and she, in concealment, gives flow to each and every one of the days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:17: And there are six days in Atzilut, which are the six extremities from Chesed to Yesod, which performed the whole work of creation, of whom it is said (Exodus 31:17), "for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth" - it does not say "with six," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 247a) - and of these he says, "and there are other six days that stand within the holy circle and are unified in the holy point." And he says "holy circle," for these are the six extremities, the reality of the circle, and it is holy, in the place of holiness in Atzilut, and the Shechinah is an inner point to them, from which they nurse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:18: And behold, on the day of Shabbat, Malchut, who is below a hidden point, ascends above into Atzilut, and what was a hidden point now spreads its light, and all the days are hidden within her, and she, with her abundant light, covers them - and this is what he says, "once Shabbat enters, then that point ascends and is crowned and unified above, and all are hidden within her." And this is what is explained in the Tikkunim which I copied above, that on the weekdays the conduct is through Metatron, and on the day of Shabbat the conduct is through the light of Atzilut, which is the Tree of Life.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:19: And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 75b), concerning the matter (Ezekiel 46:1), "the gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut the six working days, but on the Sabbath day," and so on - and the summary of his intent is that the gate of the inner court is the light of Atzilut, and it is shut during the six working days, which is the conduct through Metatron, and on the day of Shabbat it is opened and the six working days have no rule at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:20: And he further says on: and all the days, all of them cleave to the day of Shabbat and are nourished from there, for then, on the day of Shabbat, all the gates are open, and rest is found for all, above and below. And this discourse is explained by what was explained in the discourse in Parashat Vayakhel, which we wrote, that on the day of Shabbat the six days are hidden within the point, and the point, which is the light of the Shechinah in Atzilut, shines for them, and from her they nurse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:21: And relevant to our exposition is what is said in the discourse in Parashat Vayakhel: Israel, holy, and all those who occupy themselves with holiness all the days of the week, are unified - all those six days, in those six days within, which are unified in that point. The intent is that they bind the six weekdays, which are in Metatron, six chambers, to the six sefirot of the Structure that are in Atzilut, so that the light of Atzilut shine within them - and this is certainly through the intention of prayer, as explained in Parashat Pekudei, that through the intention of the blessings of the Shema and the Amidah prayer, the chambers are bound and shine from the light of Atzilut - and through this we separate the good from the evil, and the good is sanctified in the good light that is in Atzilut, and through this they are guarded from the evil.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:22: And the reason is that the six days, even though they are in Atzilut, do not have the actual holiness of the day of Shabbat - rather, during the six weekdays, when the conduct is below, even the six supernal extremities that are in Atzilut nurse from the point, and each and every day rules with its own dominion - Chesed on day one, Gevurah on day two, and so on - and the point is hidden within them, unlike on the day of Shabbat, when the point spreads its light, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:23: And the reason we need to bind the six lower days to the six upper ones is that during the six weekdays, labor was permitted because the conduct is through the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil - and this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise about in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 106b), where he said that Metatron rules over the six weekdays, which are "chulin" of impurity and "chulin" of purity - and this literally means the six days outside are "chulin" of impurity, which are the thirty-nine labors, and "chulin" of purity are the six days within, from the good in Metatron - and "chulin" of impurity and "chulin" of purity both rule together, and therefore labor was permitted. And Israel was warned to sanctify itself, as the verse says (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy" - namely, that they sanctify the pure "chulin" with the light of the holiness of Atzilut, which is entirely holy and has no contact with the profane, and shine, in the six supernal days, the holiness into the six lower days, and through this they are sanctified. And the light of Shabbat, which is the gate facing east, even though it is shut during the six working days, Israel draws from the light of the six sefirot in Atzilut to sanctify what is profane. And along these lines they explained there (Zohar, Parashat Noach, page 75b), that although we say it is shut for six days, the intent is not that the light of Atzilut is entirely sealed off, for this would indicate the removal of providence - rather, the supernal light is hidden within, and it is like the seat of a king who is in his palace, within, and commands his servants to do such and such - it follows that whatever is done is all by the king's command. My teacher, peace be upon him, further explained that it is like a parable of a king who sometimes uses vessels of silver or vessels of copper, and sometimes vessels of gold - and the meaning of the parable is understood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:24: And concerning the reality of the holiness of the six weekdays explained, they said, of blessed memory, in the Mechilta (Parashat Yitro), in these words: "remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy" - remember it from the first day of the week, that if a fine portion comes your way, prepare it for the sake of Shabbat. Rabbi Yitzchak says, do not count [the days] the way others count, but count for the sake of Shabbat - to this point. And the intent of the first Tanna and Rabbi Yitzchak both aim at one thing, to explain what this "remembering" is, and further, the extra word "et" mentioned in the verse. And to this he said that the intent is to remember the holiness of Shabbat all six days, that if a fine portion comes your way, prepare it for Shabbat - and just as, physically, one prepares and sanctifies a fine portion for Shabbat, so shall he prepare his soul that the holiness of Shabbat rest upon it - and the reason is that Shabbat is the example of the World to Come, and as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, likened this world and the World to Come to the eve of Shabbat and Shabbat, saying (Avodah Zarah 3a), whoever toils on the eve of Shabbat shall eat on Shabbat, but whoever does not toil on the eve of Shabbat, what shall he eat on Shabbat?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:25: And so they also said in the Mechilta (Parashat Ki Tisa), "for I the LORD sanctify you" (Exodus 31:13) - they said, of blessed memory: "for I the LORD sanctify you" for the World to Come, like the holiness of Shabbat in this world - we find we learn that it is a foretaste of the holiness of the World to Come; and so it says (Psalms 92:1), "a psalm, a song for the Sabbath day" - for the world that is entirely Sabbath - to this point. And the plain sense of the discourse, saying "like the holiness of Shabbat in this world," is intended to resolve the understanding of the verse, which says (Exodus 31:13), "you shall keep My Sabbaths, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I the LORD sanctify you," and afterward it says (ibid.), "and you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you," and so on. And two things should be noticed: first, how do we know that He sanctifies us because we keep the Sabbath, for He sanctified us through all the commandments, as we bless in all the commandments, "who has sanctified us with His commandments"; and further, that it is superfluous, since it already says afterward, "and you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you." Therefore he explained that the meaning of "for I the LORD sanctify you" is to give a reason for the keeping of Shabbat - and this is "for I the LORD sanctify you" for the World to Come, like the holiness of Shabbat in this world - meaning, just as I have sanctified you with the holiness of Shabbat in this world, I am destined to sanctify you in the World to Come. And the holiness of Shabbat in this world is that through a person's keeping the Shabbat according to its law, he shall feel an addition of soul within his soul - and this is "va-yinafash" (Exodus 31:17), explained by them, of blessed memory (Beitzah 16a) - and it is a delight for the soul and the body, to the point that they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 57b), that Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the foretaste of the World to Come - for the rest and delight the righteous feel in it is one-sixtieth of that wondrous delight. And the reason is that in this world, because of its physicality, we cannot attain more than this, for the soul is clothed in this material body - but once the soul strips off this turbid garment, it shall attain the delight of the World to Come in its completeness - and this is his saying, we find we learn that it is a foretaste of the holiness of the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:26: And through this we shall understand what the verse says afterward, "between Me and the children of Israel it is a sign forever" - and the intent is that Shabbat is a sign and proof for us forever, of a world that is wholly long [everlasting], for from the foretaste of this rest will come the rest that is to come. And further, just as Shabbat comes after six days, so after six thousand years the world exists, and one is destroyed, resembling Shabbat - for just as the six days rest on Shabbat, so all six thousand years rest during the one that is destroyed; and just as during the six days one must prepare for Shabbat, whether in the matter of food or in deed, as will be further explained - so, if he does not repair his deeds in this world, he has nothing to eat in the World to Come - and this is what he says, so I am destined to sanctify you in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:27: It follows that the verse is connected with what precedes it, "that you may know," and so on, "and you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you" - and in keeping the day that is holy, we shall know that He, blessed be He, is destined to sanctify us in the World to Come - and this is what he says, we find we learn that it is a foretaste of the holiness of the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:28: And having known that Shabbat is a foretaste of the holiness of the World to Come, the divine intent was to give us the holiness of Shabbat to inform us that the essential dwelling of man is not in this world - for in this world he is a stranger, as we elaborated above, and his essential place is in the world of souls, which is the World to Come - and therefore he rests from labor, which indicates the affairs of the world, and sanctifies the day of Shabbat, to show that he is sanctified and has no business with the affairs of this world - for the whole reality of holiness is separation, as is known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:29: And since this is the intent of the holiness of Shabbat, one is obligated every day to think of and remember the holiness of Shabbat, so as to remember the matters of his end, along the lines of what they said (Shabbat 153a), "repent one day before your death; let him repent today," and so on - and this is what they said, "remember it from the first day of the week, that if a fine portion comes your way," and so on. And along these lines, he should remember, from the first day of the week - meaning in his youth - what he is destined to prepare, a fine portion for his soul, for the world that is entirely Shabbat and entirely long.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:30: And I heard from the honored Rabbi Avraham HaLevi, may his light shine, that concerning this Shammai said (Beitzah 16a), "from the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbat" - for six days are sixty years, which is the lifespan of most people, and "from the first day of your week," which is the first day, meaning the first ten years, one must prepare provisions for his journey. And concerning this it is said (Exodus 20:9), "six days you shall labor, and do all your work" - and it says "all your work" [melachtecha], with the added possessive letters implying abundance for you specifically - meaning, concerning the spiritual work, the work of Torah and commandments, which is yours and not for another - unlike the other physical labors, all of which will remain for someone else. And so too concerning the manna (Exodus 16:26), "six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, which is the Sabbath, there shall be none" - which alludes to the world that is entirely Shabbat, where there is no performance of Torah and commandments, but only the receiving of reward, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained, whoever toils on the eve of Shabbat shall eat on Shabbat, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:31: And Rabbi Yitzchak said, do not count the way others count, but count for the sake of Shabbat - he gave another, very easy remembrance for all the days, for the remembrance of "if a fine portion comes your way" only applies sometimes, sometimes it comes, sometimes it does not - and therefore he said that one should count for the sake of Shabbat, counting on the first day, "today is the first day of the [week toward] Shabbat," "today is the second day of the Shabbat," "the third day of the Shabbat," and so on - it follows that he mentions the name "Shabbat" every single day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:32: And according to what was explained above, that all the days nurse from the day of Shabbat, that the day of Shabbat is the central point around which the circle of the six days revolves, like this*** - it follows that Shabbat is the root of the root of all six days of the week, and therefore, every single day, he is obligated to flow into it from the holiness of Shabbat, as will be explained. And for this reason Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise in the wording of the discourse I copied above, from Parashat Vayakhel, saying "the days of Shabbat, which are the days of the week, stand for Israel" - behold, he called them "days of the week" and "days of Shabbat" - and the reason, as explained, is that the point, which is Shabbat, is hidden within the days of the week, and therefore they are called "days of Shabbat."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:33: And so I found that Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, peace be upon him, wrote that the day of Shabbat is the central point of a circle, in these words: the whole of creation and all existing things the Holy One, blessed be He, created are all the secret of a wheel, and He created everything at one point, which is the secret of Shabbat, and it is the secret of the reality of the "eye" of every wheel - and with the presence of Shabbat, which is the secret of the point of every wheel, the six weekdays are found around her, and Shabbat, in the middle, is called holy, has no mate, and is the source of all flow and all goodness for the circle - and there is no wheel that does not have the secret of Shabbat, and the six weekdays all revolve in the circle at a necessary measure, upon which nothing may be added and from which nothing may be subtracted, for according to the measure of the middle point, so are the six measures around it around the circle, and all are called the "chalal" [hollow/space] of the circle, and it is called "chalal" from the language of "chilul" [profanation], and "chilul" is from the language of "chalal" [corpse/pierced], and all is one language - for once the central "eye" departs, all are found hollow, profaned, and pierced - for one finds a "chalal" [corpse] once its soul has already departed from it, and the body is found hollow, without the central point - and this is the secret of "six days are profane and the seventh day is holy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:34: And behold, from the reason the Rabbi, of blessed memory, wrote, there is support and reinforcement for what I have written, that one must flow from the holiness of the day of Shabbat into each and every day, since the point is the sustaining of the six, and the six are six measures around the point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:35: And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, that concerning this they said, of blessed memory (Shabbat 69b): one who walks in the wilderness and does not know when the day of Shabbat is, counts seven days from the day he took notice of his forgetting, and sanctifies the seventh, performing kiddush and havdalah. Behold, it is explicit that he is permitted to observe a Shabbat even though it is not truly Shabbat - and this is for the reason that the central point, which is Shabbat, accompanies all of them, flowing into them, and each and every day has some portion of Shabbat within it - and therefore, on each and every day, one does not perform labor beyond what is needed for his sustenance, because every day is in doubt of being Shabbat.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:36: And concerning the practical matter, we can say that this world resembles the wilderness, and a person in it is driven from the place of his rest, the rest of the soul - and in this world, being drawn after the darkness by the counsel of his inclination, he has forgotten the day of Shabbat, the day that is entirely Shabbat, which is the world of souls where his essential dwelling is. And therefore, from the day he took notice of his forgetting, and wishes to return in repentance, he must keep his garments clean always, and think every day that it is Shabbat, lest that very day he happen upon the world that is entirely Shabbat, as they said, "repent one day before your death" - and therefore he should not do labor beyond what is needed for his daily sustenance, as one who happens to be on the road, for perhaps he has life only for that day alone, and it is not fitting that he toil and worry over a world that is not his - as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 49:11), "and leave their wealth to others," and likewise (ibid. 39:7), "he heaps up riches, and does not know who shall gather them" - and they said (Gittin 47a) that Reish Lakish left behind a kav of turmeric, which is saffron, and read over it, "and leave their wealth to others."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:37: And further they said in Tractate Eruvin (54a), in these words: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda, sharp one, snatch and eat, snatch and drink, for the world we depart from is like a wedding feast. Rav said to Rav Hamnuna, my son, if you have [wealth], do good for yourself, for there is no pleasure in Sheol, and death does not delay; and if you say, I will leave it for my children - who will tell you the law in Sheol [whether they'll benefit]? And if you say, I will leave it for my sons and daughters - people are like the grass of the field: some sprout and some wither - to this point. And Rashi explained: "snatch and eat" - if you have money to benefit yourself, do not wait until tomorrow, lest you die and then have no enjoyment; "for the world we depart from" is our reading, "is like a wedding feast" - today it exists, and tomorrow it is gone; "if you have" - money; "and death does not delay" - a postponement, for a person dies suddenly; "the law" - sustenance; "who will tell you" - if it remains in their hands, perhaps they will lose it; "some sprout and some wither" - meaning, as they grow, their livelihood and wealth grow with them, and you need not worry about them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:38: And he must sanctify the seventh - that one day a week he sanctify entirely to the LORD, corresponding to the many days that went by in vain in service to a strange god within him - and we have already elaborated in the Gate of Fear (chapter 9) that they exact payment from him in Gehinnom, day for day, one for two - therefore he must sanctify one day to the service of his Owner with the holiness of the day of Shabbat, for the holiness of speech and the abstention from labor that nullifies a person's cleaving to his Owner - and therefore it is good that he seclude himself in a special place and sanctify all his senses properly. And the day of Shabbat alone does not suffice for the penitent, for the day of Shabbat was given to him had he not sinned - but after he has sinned and blemished so many days, he must sanctify at least one day a week to the LORD, and if possible, more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:39: And so he says in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Acharei Mot), that there were two merchants who would separate themselves from settled life two days each week to occupy themselves with Torah, in these words there, concerning Rabbi Chiya, who was on the road and found two men in a rocky valley, and said, I approached them and said to them, what is your business in this place? They said, we are merchants, and two days a week we separate ourselves from settled life and occupy ourselves with Torah, because people do not leave us alone every single day. I said, happy is your portion - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:40: And holiness is in moderation, so that every person can fulfill it and persevere in it - for if he wishes to separate himself all the days of the week, he will not persevere, and will end up idle from everything - and therefore it is fitting to grasp holiness little by little, and learn from these men of deeds mentioned, "what profit has a man of all his labor which he takes under the sun" - and he has nothing in his world except what he sanctifies and separates from the affairs of this world, and cleaves to the Name, blessed be He.
